name: Runtime_InitIwramAndInterrupts
algorithm: Disables interrupts, DMA-copies the 5120-byte relocated IWRAM payload (ROM 0x08000770 -> RAM 0x03000000), records the IWRAM base pointer at 0x03007ffc, DMA-copies the 56-byte (14-entry) interrupt-dispatch pointer table (ROM 0x08007320 -> RAM 0x030000e0), clears REG_DISPSTAT, arms REG_KEYCNT, enables VBlank+Keypad in REG_IE, then re-enables IME.
evidence: DMA control words 0x84000500 (0x500 words = 5120 bytes) and 0x8400000e (0x0e words = 56 bytes) match, byte-for-byte, the 5120-byte 'relocated_iwram_payload' group and the 56-byte 'iwram_dispatch_pointers_08007320' table both recorded independently in games/gs1/asm/classification.json and games/gs1/asm/executable_gaps/index.json.

The dispatch table's 14 pointer values are 0x08003009 (Func_08003008 + thumb bit, i.e. runtime/dispatch/reserved_no_op_f.c) repeated, with one override to 0x08003811 (Input_InitKeyIrq + thumb bit) -- consistent with initializing a default-no-op interrupt dispatch table.
Register addresses 0x04000208/0x04000200/0x04000004/0x04000132 match REG_IME/REG_IE/REG_DISPSTAT/REG_KEYCNT as already named in games/gs1/recon/en/main/serial_runtime_family.h for sibling owners.
credible_shapes_tried: plain per-field volatile struct stores through a DMA3-style pointer (u32 or pointer-typed fields, with or without an intermediate 'iwram'/'dma' local variable): 114 candidate bytes vs 112 reference, 56 differing halfwords -- closest length match found; kept as the current draft

compile-time-constant compound-literal struct assignment for one or both DMA setups: for an all-constant compound literal the compiler emits a genuine paired `ldmia r3!, {..}` / `stmia r2!, {..}` (movmem12b), confirming empirically this is the only Thumb pathway that emits a multi-register stmia at all; 106-118 candidate bytes, 52-58 differing halfwords, and an extra callee-saved register (r7) not present in the reference

raw u32* pointer with sequential post-increment stores (*p++ = a; *p++ = b; *p = c;): each store lowers to its own single-register `stmia rX!, {rY}` (Thumb's only way to get a post-incrementing SImode store), never merging into one three-register stmia; 122 candidate bytes, 60 differing halfwords
compiler_backend_evidence: Independently confirmed by reading alchemy-gcc/gs1cc/gcc/config/arm/arm.md and arm.c (same files cited in 08003e10.json): the only Thumb machine pattern that ever emits literal multi-register 'stmia' text is movmem12b/movmem8b (thumb_expand_movstrqi, arm.md ~5111-5155; thumb_output_move_mem_multiple, arm.c ~9425-9469), and both cases in thumb_output_move_mem_multiple emit ldmia immediately before stmia as one indivisible RTL insn -- it can only represent a genuine memory-to-memory block copy, never a lone grouped store of independently-computed register values. The generic 'store_multiple' expander and *stmsi/*stmsi_postinc patterns (arm.md ~4997-5075) are gated 'TARGET_ARM' with no Thumb counterpart. The reference's two `stmia r3!, {r0, r1, r2}` stores are each fed by three independently loaded registers (three separate pc-relative ldr's / a register move, no preceding ldmia), which is the same structural shape 08003e10.json already documented as unemittable from ordinary C on this compiler route.
remaining: The 56 differing halfwords are concentrated around the two DMA descriptor writes: the reference's standalone, unpaired three-register stmia appears unreachable from any ordinary field-store, aggregate-store, or pointer-store C shape on this Thumb/GCC 2.96 route (see compiler_backend_evidence). The draft also does not reproduce the reference's r5/r6 callee-saved register allocation (push {r5,r6,lr} / pop {r5,r6}; pop {r0}; bx r0) for the REG_IME address and the shared IWRAM-base value -- every local-variable shape tried caused the compiler to either drop the callee-saved registers entirely or synthesize 0x03000000 via shift instead of a literal-pool load, rather than matching the reference's register-reuse pattern. Candidate length remains 114 vs 112 target bytes.
notes: Cold-start owner: games/gs1/recon/en/main/0800300c.c did not exist before this pass; games/gs1/asm/0800300c.s (the proven byte-exact retained assembly) was reconstructed by hand from its literal pool and cross-checked against a direct hex dump of roms/gs1-en.gba at 0x0800300c.
No inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, forbidden ABI, copied instruction bytes, or compiler modification was used.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes.
